Lab kit example

One round, written to the spec

A concept, seven steps, and a check-in. Copy this file to start a lab.

This deck exists to show the lab spec working. Read docs/03-playbooks/arduino-lab/instruction-spec.md first.

Every lab starts by finding the parts.

Do it · two minutes

Find your parts

  1. Take out the breadboard, power module, and 9V battery
  2. Take out the UNO board, USB cable, and jumper wires
  3. Take out one red LED, one 220 Ω resistor, two buttons
  4. Take out the fan blade, the motor, and the servo

2:00

T to start

Names come from the parts glossary.

One idea behind every circuit.

Circuits from zero

Every circuit is a loop

  1. Electricity leaves +, comes back to -No way back, nothing flows
  2. Your part sits in the loopIt lights up, spins, or beeps
  3. Break the loop anywhere, it all stopsThat's all a switch does
  4. Something in the loop has to slow itWith nothing there, it's a short

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

A concept slide fills in on its own.

Build one.

Light an LED · step 1 of 7

Put the power module on the end

Take the power module. Line up its + pins with the red lines and its - pins with the blue lines. Press it into the left end of the breadboard until its pins sink into the rails.

  1. It sits flat across both rails+ on red, - on blue

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

Backwards reverses the power.

Light an LED · step 2 of 7

Set both jumpers to 5V

Find the two small caps (jumpers) on the module, one on each side. Pull each cap off and push it back on over the pins labelled 5V.

  1. Both jumpers on 5VNot 3.3V, and not OFF

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

Both OFF means nothing turns on.

Light an LED · step 3 of 7

Plug in the 9V battery

Check that the module's light is off. Snap the battery cable onto the 9V battery if it isn't already, then push its round plug into the round jack on the module.

  1. The light stays off for nowThe switch is still off

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

Never more than 9V.

Light an LED · step 4 of 7

Add the resistor

Take one resistor labelled 220. Bend both legs down. Plug one leg into any hole in the top + rail (red line) and the other leg into hole a10.

  1. One leg in the rail, one in row 10Each leg in its own spot

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

It works either way around.

Light an LED · step 5 of 7

Add the LED

Take one red LED. Plug its long leg into hole c10 and its short leg into hole c11.

  1. The long leg shares row 10 with the resistorThat's how they connect

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

Long leg is +.

Light an LED · step 6 of 7

Connect the short leg to ground

Take a jumper wire. Plug one end into hole a11 and the other end into any hole in the top - rail (blue line).

  1. Row 11 now runs to the - railThe loop is closed

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

The - rail is ground.

Light an LED · step 7 of 7

Trace it, then switch on

Run your finger along the path: + rail, resistor, row 10, LED, row 11, jumper, - rail. Then press the module's power switch.

  1. The module light and your LED turn onDark LED? Flip it around

Fills in on its own. One press lands the rest; the next press moves on.

Hands off after this step.

Check in.

Check in

Why your LED lit up

  1. It lit upThe loop is complete: +, resistor, LED, back to -
  2. Now pull one wire outDark. No loop, nothing flows
  3. Why the resistor?It slows the flow so the LED doesn't burn out
  4. Habits you just usedPower off while wiring, trace before switching on

Ask first, then press.

That's the round.
